_meta.indication: POMALYST is indicated for patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least two prior therapies including lenalidomide and bortezomib and have demonstrated disease progression on or within 60 days of completion of the last therapy; approval is based on response rate

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, open-label study evaluating POMALYST alone versus POMALYST plus low-dose dexamethasone (patients in the POMALYST-alone arm were allowed to add low-dose dexamethasone upon disease progression)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with relapsed multiple myeloma refractory to their last therapy who had received lenalidomide and bortezomib; median of 5 prior therapies
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR), based on assessments by the Independent Review Adjudication Committee
pivotal_trials.n: 221 patients randomized (POMALYST N=108; POMALYST/Low dose Dex N=113)
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 29.2% (95% CI 21.0, 38.5) with POMALYST/Low dose Dex versus 7.4% (95% CI 3.3, 14.1) with POMALYST alone; median duration of response 7.4 months (95% CI 5.1, 9.2) for the combination

nct_ctgov.title: MTD, Safety, and Efficacy of Pomalidomide (CC-4047) Alone or With Low-dose Dexamethasone in Patients With Relapsed and Refractory Multiple Myeloma

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=30%): fatigue and asthenia, neutropenia, anemia, constipation, nausea, diarrhea, dyspnea, upper-respiratory tract infections, back pain and pyrexia. Neutropenia was the most frequent Grade 3/4 event (47% POMALYST alone, 38% combination); anemia Grade 3/4 22%/21%; pneumonia Grade 3/4 16%/23%.
target_moa: Pomalidomide, an analogue of thalidomide, is an immunomodulatory agent (IMiD) with antineoplastic activity; in vitro it inhibited proliferation and induced apoptosis of hematopoietic tumor cells and synergized with dexamethasone

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY and VENOUS THROMBOEMBOLISM — POMALYST is a thalidomide analogue contraindicated in pregnancy (a known human teratogen); DVT and PE occur in patients treated with POMALYST

rems.type: POMALYST is available only through a restricted distribution program called POMALYST REMS, required to mitigate the risk of teratogenicity; prescribers and pharmacies must be certified and patients enrolled with documentation of safe-use conditions

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this drug is not the first in its class and the safety profile is similar to that of other drugs approved for this indication

description.text: Added new indication for adult patients with AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma after failure of HAART (accelerated approval)

citations.quote: This "Prior Approval" supplemental new drug application provides for the addition of a new indication for the treatment of adult patients with AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma (KS) after failure of highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) with associated changes and modifications to the Prescribing Information (PI) and proposed modifications to the approved REMS for POMALYST (pomalidomide).

description.text: Added new indication for treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma in HIV-negative patients (accelerated approval)

citations.quote: This "Prior Approval" supplemental new drug application provides for the addition of a new indication for the treatment of Kaposi's Sarcoma in patients who are HIV-negative and modifications to the Prescribing Information (PI) and proposed modifications to the approved REMS for POMALYST (pomalidomide).

description.text: Updated labeling with pediatric study results (PBTC-043, BRN-001, MPK-004); no new indication added

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA revises the prescribing information (PI) to update Section 8, Use in Specific Populations, subsection 8.4 Pediatric Use, and Section 12, Clinical Pharmacology, subsection 12.3 Pharmacokinetics, to include the results from the pediatric studies PBTC-043 and BRN-001 and an integrated pharmacokinetic analysis report (MPK-004) conducted as part of the June 26, 2019, Amended Written Request (Amendment #2).

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate — approval is based on response rate; clinical benefit (improvement in survival or symptoms) has not been verified

citations.quote: POMALYST is indicated for patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least two prior therapies including lenalidomide and bortezomib and have demonstrated disease progression or within 60 days of completion of the last therapy. Approval is based on response rate [see *Clinical Studies* (14.1)]. Clinical benefit, such as improvement in survival or symptoms, has not been verified.

confirmatory_requirement.text: PMR 2006-1: Conduct a randomized controlled trial (CC-4047-MM-007) that isolates and demonstrates the efficacy and safety of POMALYST in patients with previously treated multiple myeloma

orphan_indication.text: Pomalidomide has orphan drug designation for this indication and is therefore exempt from PREA requirements

citations.quote: Pomalidomide has orphan drug designation and is therefore exempt from PREA requirements.
Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

summary.text: POMALYST received accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 based on response rate from two Phase 2 trials (CC-4047-MM-002 and IFM-2009-02); the drug had orphan drug designation (exempting it from PREA), and a confirmatory randomized controlled trial (CC-4047-MM-007) was required as a postmarketing requirement to verify clinical benefit.

citations.quote: We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved under the provisions of accelerated approval regulations (21 CFR 314.510), effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling text.

The recommendation for accelerated approval is based on the two Phase 2 clinical trials, CC-4047-MM-002 and IFM-2009-02, in which pomalidomide and dexamethasone showed overall response responses rate of 29% and 34%, respectively. The efficacy of single-agent pomalidomide in CC-4047-MM-002 was 7%.
Pomalidomide has orphan drug designation and is therefore exempt from PREA requirements.

requirement.text: PMR 2006-4: Conduct a clinical trial in patients with baseline hepatic impairment to determine the influence of hepatic impairment on PK and safety of POMALYST

citations.quote: PMR 2006-4 Conduct a clinical trial, per FDA guidance [Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Hepatic Function: Study Design, Data Analysis, and Impact on Dosing and Labeling], in patients with baseline hepatic impairment to determine the influence of hepatic impairment on the pharmacokinetics (PK) and safety of Pomalyst (pomalidomide).

requirement.text: PMR 2006-6: Conduct a clinical trial to determine the effect of CYP3A inhibition on POMALYST pharmacokinetics

citations.quote: PMR 2006-6 Conduct a clinical trial, per FDA guidance [Drug Interaction Studies—Study Design, Data Analysis, Implications for Dosing, and Labeling Recommendations], in order to determine the effect of CYP3A inhibition, which may increase drug exposure and thereby drug toxicity, on Pomalyst (pomalidomide) pharmacokinetics.

requirement.text: PMR 2006-7: Conduct a food effect clinical trial to determine the effect of food on PK of POMALYST (patients >60 years old using the commercial formulation)

citations.quote: PMR 2006-7 Conduct a food effect clinical trial, per FDA guidance [Food-effect Bioavailability and Fed Bioequivalence Studies], in order to determine the effect of food on the pharmacokinetics of Pomalyst (pomalidomide). The trial should be conducted in patients age > 60 years old using the commercial formulation of pomalidomide.

requirement.text: PMR 2006-8: Conduct a randomized controlled trial (MM-003) of pomalidomide plus dexamethasone in previously treated multiple myeloma to determine the safety profile versus an arm without pomalidomide

citations.quote: PMR 2006-8 Conduct a randomized controlled trial (MM-003) of the combination of pomalidomide and dexamethasone in patients with previously treated multiple myeloma, to determine the safety profile of pomalidomide and dexamethasone combination as compared to a treatment arm without pomalidomide.

requirement.text: PMR 2006-9: Conduct a QT prolongation trial to assess the effect of POMALYST on the QT interval

citations.quote: PMR 2006-9 Conduct a QT prolongation trial, per FDA guidance [E14 Clinical Evaluation of QT/QTc interval Prolongation and Proarrhythmic Potential for Non-Antiarrhythmic Drugs], to assess the effect of Pomalyst (pomalidomide) on the QT interval.

requirement.text: PMC 2006-10: Conduct a clinical trial to determine the effects of a CYP1A2 inducer (such as montelukast) on the PK of POMALYST

citations.quote: PMC 2006-10 Conduct a clinical trial, per FDA guidance [Drug Interaction Studies—Study Design, data Analysis, Implications for Dosing, and Labeling Recommendations], in order to determine the effects of a CYP1A2 inducer (such as montelukast) on the PK of Pomalyst (pomalidomide). CYP1A2 induction may decrease Pomalyst (pomalidomide) exposure and result in diminished efficacy.
